_comment: The rule-carrier registry — proposal 0027, `a reduced rule stays reduced`.
A rule an incident REDUCED to one carrier is registered here with the spellings its other
carriers used. Those spellings may then appear only in the carrier, or beside a citation of it.
This registry covers ONLY the rules listed below. Every other rule in this repository is
unregistered and therefore uncovered, and nothing can audit that — a rule has no token, which is
proposal 0020's theorem. The arrears are named rather than pretended away.
`scope` and `exclude` are path PREFIXES, not globs. `exclude` wins. The record layer is excluded
globally because it legitimately quotes retired sentences forever.

rules.summary: What CI runs is the set the workspace manifest YIELDS — its own declared recipes plus those its composed packs contribute, namespaced by pack — and not the list it declares. Landed at milestone 7 session 5; cli/recipe-set.mjs is the one carrier of the set and CI calls it rather than enumerating a manifest.
rules._tells_comment: Every tell below was MEASURED against the pre-sweep tree (27705ae), not invented. Two plural variants were written from memory, matched nothing, and the dead-tell audit rejected them on its first run — `invented is a claim`, and the audit is what makes that checkable rather than a maxim.
tells: from the manifest and runs each one

rules.summary: The A/B clause's subject is the mandates core SHIPS that an arm actually receives — the kernel's, plus the artifact mandates reachable in a built arm — of which the judgement-only rows are a part. Widened 2026-08-28 on the maintainer's ruling, from a narrower reading that named the judgement rows alone. The narrower reading could not survive measurement: `vendor --host` carries `core/skills/` not at all, so all five judgement rows reach nothing in a vendored arm.
rules._tells_comment: Every tell below is a LINE-LEVEL fragment verified to match at 39175b50 with `git grep -F`, which is the granularity the scanner actually reads. A FIRST CUT OF THIS ENTRY REGISTERED FOUR SENTENCE-LEVEL SPELLINGS AND THREE OF THEM MATCHED NOTHING: each spanned a line break — two across `io.log` string literals, one across a `# ` comment wrap, one across a Markdown wrap — and they read alive only because the carrier below quotes them on single lines. The pre-commit checkpoint caught it, and the defect is worth more than the repair: the claim `every tell was measured` was itself written from memory, inside the registry whose whole subject is that discipline. A FIFTH spelling exists at .portulan/handoffs/2026-08-26-b-the-denominator-was-a-set-the-author-drew.md and is deliberately NOT registered: it spans a line break so no tell could match it, and it sits under a globally excluded path where it can never be a finding — registering it would add a DEAD TELL and redden this rail.
rules._coverage_comment: WHAT THIS RULE DOES NOT COVER, stated because the sentence it replaced overclaimed. `exclude` is global, so `docs/milestones/`, `docs/plan.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and the record layer are outside every rule here — and `docs/milestones/` is precisely where the fourth carrier sat and survived a sweep. This registration stops a fifth appearing IN THE REGISTERED SCOPE; it cannot see one appearing where the fourth was. Nor does the dead-tell audit protect this rule the way it protects rule 1: the carrier quotes all four spellings, so every tell stays alive whatever the citing files do, and the audit can only redden if somebody edits the carrier's own list. That is a trade, not a feature.
